Modified assessment incorporating SLOOS insights:
- SLOOS (July 2024) indicates the bank credit channel remains a headwind: net tightening of standards and weaker demand for C&I loans to firms of all sizes; CRE standards remained tight with notably weak demand (especially office) and concerns about valuations/collateral. Nonprice terms stayed stringent.
- Residential real estate: standards largely unchanged across many RRE categories, but demand remained soft; HELOC standards tightened.
- Consumer credit: banks reported further tightening for credit cards, auto, and other consumer loans, including wider loan rate spreads, higher minimum required credit scores, and higher minimum payment requirements; some uptick in delinquencies.
- Drivers cited by banks: a still-uncertain economic outlook, reduced risk tolerance, collateral valuation pressures (notably CRE), and concerns about borrowers’ financial positions.
- Implications for the FOMC statement: While the 50 bp cut and “greater confidence” on disinflation are dovish and supportive of risk assets, SLOOS shows credit supply/demand frictions that can restrain growth and amplify downside risks, consistent with a cautious posture. Easing policy alongside ongoing QT and robust standing facilities helps, but tight bank lending conditions temper the otherwise positive tone.

Net: still positive versus neutral given disinflation progress and policy easing, but SLOOS-related credit headwinds warrant a further notch down in sentiment from prior.
